name: SearchWrench – Local SEO & Security Check
author: searchwrench

sections.description:
Your customers search Google and ask AI assistants like ChatGPT who to call. Both read the same hidden details on your site: page titles, descriptions, social share previews and your business information (schema). On most small-business sites those are missing or generic.

SearchWrench scans your home page and shows:

  • Your SEO score out of 100
  • The issues that matter most, worst first, in plain English
  • Which issues SearchWrench Autopilot can fix for you (marked Auto) and which are quick fixes you can make yourself (marked Tip)

The scan is free and needs no account.

Optional: SearchWrench Autopilot

Autopilot is a paid service on searchwrench.com. When you connect it, it writes page titles, meta descriptions, social share (Open Graph) tags and LocalBusiness schema into your site through this plugin, then re-checks every week and keeps them right. Nothing changes in your theme or page design, and deactivating the plugin removes every change instantly.

Connecting uses WordPress’s own application passwords (built in since WordPress 5.6). You approve the connection on your own site and can revoke it at any time under Users → Profile.

Security Watchdog (free)

A weekly check of the things that most often get small business sites hacked, with a plain-English list of what to fix, worst first:

  • WordPress, plugin and theme updates waiting
  • WordPress core files that differ from the official copy
  • PHP code files hiding in the uploads folder
  • A user called “admin”, too many administrators
  • The dashboard code editor switched on, error messages shown to visitors, no https
  • Failed logins in the last 7 days

It runs on your own server and needs no account. It emails your site’s admin address only when a new serious problem appears (you can turn that off). Optional login protection makes an address wait 15 minutes after 5 failed logins; addresses are kept only as a one-way code that expires after 15 minutes.

Keep your site updated (free)

Out-of-date plugins are the most common way small business sites get hacked. On the Security screen you can:

  • Turn on Keep WordPress, plugins and themes updated automatically. It is off until you switch it on. It uses WordPress’s own automatic updates for security releases, plugins and themes; big WordPress version upgrades are left to you.
  • Click Update everything now to install every plugin and theme update that is waiting.

After every update the plugin checks that your home page still loads, keeps a short history of what changed, and emails your site’s admin address if the home page stops loading.

Build pages (free drafts)

People search for a service in their town (“water heater repair in Mason”). Pick one of the services and towns your site already mentions, choose page or blog post, and SearchWrench writes a helpful local page from your own site’s words: no made-up prices, guarantees, licences or reviews. It is saved as a draft so you can review it before you publish. 5 free drafts a month per site.

Tap-to-call

Enter your business phone number on the SearchWrench screen and it becomes a tap-to-call link wherever it appears on your site, so visitors on a phone can call you with one tap. It only links that one number, never changes anything else, and needs no account. Leave the field empty to turn it off.

Weekly service posts (Autopilot)

If you connect Autopilot, it can publish one new blog post a week about a service your site already offers, in a town your site already names. Posts are written only from what your own site says (no made-up prices, guarantees or reviews), appear under Posts like any other post, and can be edited or deleted. Switch this off any time on the SearchWrench screen.

Rankings are never guaranteed.

External services

This plugin connects to the SearchWrench service at https://searchwrench.com.

  • What is sent, and when: only when an administrator clicks “Scan my site” (or “Scan again”) on the SearchWrench admin page, the plugin sends your site’s home page address, the word “wordpress” and the plugin version to https://searchwrench.com/api/plugin/scan. SearchWrench then loads your public home page, the same way a search engine does, to score it. Nothing is sent automatically, and no visitor data, user data or content from your database is sent.
  • Autopilot (optional): if you choose to connect SearchWrench Autopilot, searchwrench.com calls this plugin’s REST API (namespace searchwrench/v1) with the application password you approved, to store page titles, descriptions, schema, redirects, robots.txt lines and the tap-to-call phone number, and (if weekly service posts are switched on) to publish posts through the standard WordPress REST API.
  • Build pages: only when an administrator clicks “Find my services and towns” or “Write the draft” on the Build pages screen, the plugin sends your site’s home page address, a random site code made by this plugin, the plugin version and (for a draft) the chosen service, town and page type to https://searchwrench.com/api/plugin/topics or /api/plugin/write. SearchWrench reads your public pages and this plugin’s /wp-json/searchwrench/v1/claim route (which shows only a one-way hash of the site code) to confirm the request came from your site, then returns the draft text. No visitor data, user data or database content is sent.
  • Security Watchdog: to check core files, the plugin asks WordPress.org for the official checksums of your WordPress version (https://api.wordpress.org/core/checksums/1.0/, the same request WordPress itself makes), weekly and when you click “Check now”. Nothing about your site is sent to SearchWrench by the Watchdog.
  • Terms of service: https://searchwrench.com/terms.html
  • Privacy policy: https://searchwrench.com/privacy.html
sections.installation:
1. Install from Plugins → Add New (search “SearchWrench”), or upload the zip.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open SearchWrench in the admin menu and click Scan my site.

Your site has to be public for the scan to work. Local and staging sites (localhost, .test, .local) cannot be reached from the internet.
sections.faq:
Is the scan really free?

Yes. The score and issue list are free with no account. Autopilot, which writes the fixes for you, is an optional paid service on searchwrench.com.

Does it work with Yoast SEO or Rank Math?

Yes. The scan works alongside any SEO plugin. If Yoast SEO or Rank Math is active, this plugin does not print its own canonical link, so you never get two.

What happens if I deactivate it?

Every title, description, schema block and redirect that Autopilot stored stops being printed immediately. Deleting the plugin removes its saved settings.

Is the Security Watchdog a firewall?

No. It checks your site’s setup every week and tells you what to fix, and it can slow down password guessing on the login page. It does not block traffic or scan for malware the way a full security plugin does, and it works alongside one.

Will the page builder publish anything by itself?

No. Every page or post it writes is saved as a draft. Nothing goes live until you open it and click Publish.

Does it slow my site down?

No. On the front end it only reads one saved option and prints a few tags in the page head on pages that have an Autopilot fix. The scan runs on searchwrench.com, not on your server.
sections.changelog:
2.4.0

  • Simpler first screen: one button to scan, then your score and the 3 issues that matter most.
  • After activation the SearchWrench screen opens once, and one dismissible reminder shows on the Plugins and Dashboard screens until you scan.
  • The Fix button now opens the first-month-free Autopilot offer for WordPress sites (no card needed for the free month).

2.3.0

  • New: Keep this site updated. Optional automatic updates for WordPress security releases, plugins and themes (off until you turn it on), an “Update everything now” button, a home-page check after every update, and an update history.

2.2.1

  • Clearer plugin name in the WordPress.org directory. The Upgrade link now applies the first-month-free offer for WordPress users automatically.

2.2.0

  • New: Security Watchdog. A free weekly security check with plain-English fixes, email alerts for new serious problems, and optional login protection.
  • New: Build pages. Pick a service and a town your site already names and get a local page or blog post written from your own site, saved as a draft (5 free drafts a month).

2.1.0

  • New: tap-to-call. Set your phone number and it becomes a tap-to-call link wherever it appears on your site.
  • New: optional weekly service posts published by SearchWrench Autopilot (can be switched off on the SearchWrench screen).

2.0.2

  • Settings are now stored under unique searchwrench_seo_ option names.
  • Plugin URI points to the SearchWrench home page.

2.0.1

  • All SearchWrench settings and REST routes now require an administrator (manage_options).

2.0.0

  • New: SearchWrench admin page with a free one-click SEO scan.
  • Security: schema output is encoded so it can never break out of its script tag; request paths are sanitized; redirects and robots.txt changes now need an administrator.
  • Removes the last scan result on uninstall.

1.1.0

  • Social share (Open Graph) tags and self-referencing canonical for pages managed by Autopilot.
